prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t pick a single “best” company for you without knowing where in the Phoenix area you are and what the problem is. I also don’t have live web access to pull current local ratings. That said, I can help you find a reliable HVAC contractor and avoid common pitfalls. Two quick options:

- If you want a short list of highly rated companies near you, tell me your ZIP code and whether this is an emergency (no cooling right now). I’ll then tell you what to look for and give wording you can use to contact them.  
- If you prefer to choose yourself, use the checklist and call script below when evaluating companies.

How to choose the best HVAC company (quick checklist)
- Licensing: Ask for their Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) license number and verify it online.  
- Certifications: Technicians should have EPA 608 refrigerant certification and preferably NATE certification.  
- Insurance: Confirm they carry liability and workers’ comp insurance.  
- Reviews & complaints: Check recent Google/Yelp reviews and BBB history for patterns (not single bad reviews).  
- Experience: Ask how long they’ve been servicing Phoenix-area systems and whether they work on your system brand.  
- Guarantees: Get written warranties on parts and labor and a written estimate.  
- Permits: They should obtain permits for major work and charge appropriately if required.  
- Pricing: Get at least 3 quotes for significant repairs or replacements. Extremely low quotes are often a red flag.  
- Emergency availability: Ask if they offer 24/7 service in summer and typical response time.

Questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed in Arizona? What’s your ROC number?  
- Are your technicians EPA-608 and NATE certified?  
- Do you carry liability insurance and workers’ comp? Can you email proof?  
- What is your diagnostic fee? Will it be applied to the repair cost?  
- Do you provide a written estimate and a warranty on parts and labor? How long?  
- Can you give references from customers in my neighborhood?  
- Do you pull permits for major work?  
- Do you offer financing or payment plans if I need a replacement?

Typical price ranges (Phoenix area, ballpark)
- Simple repairs (capacitor, contactor, fan motor): $150–$600  
- Refrigerant recharge (if legal and applicable): $200–$600 (depends on refrigerant type/amount)  
- Condenser/compressor replacement: $1,200–$4,000+ (varies by unit)  
- Full system replacement: $4,000–$12,000+ (brand, efficiency, ductwork)

Red flags
- No ROC number or unwillingness to provide it.  
- Pushy high-pressure sales or insisting on full replacement without diagnosing.  
- Only takes cash and no receipt or contract.  
- Very low up-front price that balloons with “extras.”

If you want, tell me:
- Your ZIP code (or neighborhood)  
- The symptoms (no cool air, blows but not cold, cycles on/off, strange noises, leak)  
- Whether it’s urgent

I’ll then help you narrow the search, suggest several well-reviewed local options (based on common regional reputations), and give a tailored list of likely causes and rough cost estimates for your issue.
